# Native Candidate Replay Benchmark (Provisional)

## Scope and Known Rotary Plant

F03b (#11824, parent F03 #11787) tests two candidate torque histories against
F06's fresh MuJoCo direct-motor replay. The fixture has one hinge, no gravity
and no contact geometry. It is a synthetic solver and replay-boundary check,
not a calibrated body or full-swing result. With SI rotary inertia
$m>0$ (kg m²), damping $c\ge0$ (N m s/rad), stiffness $k\ge0$ (N m/rad),
position $q$ (rad), velocity $v$ (rad/s), and post-limit motor torque
$\tau$ (N m), the intended dynamics are

$$
\dot q=v,\qquad m\dot v=\tau-cv-kq.
$$

The native XML specifies a hinge with axis $+y$, inertia tensor
$\operatorname{diag}(m,m,m)$ about that hinge, joint damping and spring
stiffness, a direct unit-gain motor, and RK4. Its compiled model and source
are bound by F06. No other actuator force, root control or hidden contact
wrench is introduced. The sole motor has the same hard control range as the
solver's torque bounds. The validator recomputes the actual torque and slew
residuals in their respective units, independent of solver-reported values.

## Independent Truth and Native Replay

For each interval $h=t_{i+1}-t_i$ with zero-order-held $\tau_i$, an
independent matrix exponential supplies exact synthetic truth. With

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-k/m&-c/m\end{bmatrix},\qquad
B=\begin{bmatrix}0\\1/m\end{bmatrix},
$$

the augmented exponential
$\exp\!\left(h\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\0&0\end{bmatrix}\right)$
maps $(q_i,v_i,\tau_i)$ to $(q_{i+1},v_{i+1})$. This calculation is separate
from the sparse midpoint defect, the F03a adaptive RK45 replay and MuJoCo
RK4. A closed-form double-integrator case checks its sign and units.

The original synthetic time grid must start at zero and have uniform
spacing. An explicit positive integer refinement repeats each original
post-bound torque for the corresponding native substeps. This creates the
**executed** ZOH history at the native timestep, with an unused terminal
sentinel; it does not interpolate a polynomial or retime observations. F06
binds the complete initial `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION`, actual ordered actuator
torque, model/provider, channel, input-grid and execution-policy hashes, then
steps a fresh native model without feedback callbacks or state resets.

The receipt keeps transcription defect, native-versus-exact integrator gap,
native-versus-transcription node gap, F03a RK45-versus-exact gap, observation
RMSE, torque residual and slew residual separate. Small node defect never
establishes native rollout agreement: the coarse stiff fixture has a tiny
midpoint defect but fails the independent native node-gap gate. Native
substep refinement reduces RK4's error relative to matrix-exponential truth;
the changed native input grid produces a distinct executed-input hash.
Candidate observations are sampled only at the original synthetic nodes.
Real capture clocks, marker masks and uncertainties would need explicit
post-integration observation interpolation and their own digest; input
sampling cannot stand in for a 240/359/360 Hz capture timebase.

## Benchmark Accounting and Acceptance Boundary

`benchmark_native_candidates` runs the predeclared starts serially. Each
attempt records preparation, solver/derivative work, native model creation,
bundle verification and replay, deterministic JSON receipt export, and total
time. Failed starts remain in the output and in time-to-first-accepted cost.
Cold/warm p50/p95 total time and Python-tracked peak allocation are reported
with host, platform and library versions. The receipt digest binds each
exported synthetic attempt. Python allocation is not process RSS or native
MuJoCo allocation; the fixture excludes capture preprocessing, full-body
resource loading and any private-data run. There is no hidden warmup or
parallel candidate search.

The same native validator evaluates the existing multiple-shooting adapter and
the sparse collocation spike, but their parameterizations remain unequal:
one constant torque versus one per-interval torque. Their native errors can
be checked, yet these results cannot select a production backend. Tolerances
in the tests are predeclared synthetic regression limits, not calibrated
noise or clinical/biomechanical acceptance thresholds. F03 parent still needs
the frozen D02/D03 capture protocol, full-body/contact model, comparable
candidate resources, complete time-to-accepted-capture cost and a documented
production selection. An empty-contact hinge cannot qualify native swing
ground/grip, muscles, anatomy or any of the six-engine parity gates.

Run the focused checks with
`python -m pytest tests/unit/motion_matching/test_native_candidate_benchmark.py -q`
after the merged Tools T01 pin and F06 consumer boundary are available.
During development, the Tools worktree facade was preloaded explicitly; that
override is not portable evidence. Keep this chapter and its registry entry
provisional until a reproducible native receipt is produced under the merged
dependency pin.
